extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, hearing examiners, statisticians and researchers compiling or using administrative adjudication time-and-backlog statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and measurement rules for compiling and reporting time intervals, volumes, backlog, and examiner workload for agency adjudicative proceedings (hearing, examiner decision, agency final decision). Includes definitions of start/end points, inclusion/exclusion rules, and computation methods for derived statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: 'traveled the full route' proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Study data on only those proceedings which "traveled the full route" through hearing, examiner decision, and agency final decision on the merits, and were thereby closed during the fiscal years 1958 and 1959 (the 5,403 proceedings reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include proceedings that completed the entire sequence: evidentiary hearing, examiner decision on the merits, and agency final decision on the merits. Other matters (e.g., cases not reaching agency final decision) are excluded from this particular measurement set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall time (Table 4): commencement to agency final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 4 illustrates the over-all time involved in the handling of each such case, from the date the proceeding was commenced to the date of the agency's final decision which closed the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include time involved in disposition of petitions for reopening, rehearing, or reconsideration in these overall time intervals. If a proceeding is reopened it is added to input as a new case for statistical purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing completion date (Tables 5 and 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of these tables, the hearing is considered completed on the last day on which testimony or documentary or other evidence was put into the record, whether or not oral argument on the record was to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the last day evidence was placed in the record as the hearing-completion date; subsequent oral argument (if any) does not change the 'completion' date for these measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of phases — management point of view (three basic divisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: From an agency management point of view consider: (1) 'administrative processing' — period from original filing to assignment to an examiner for hearing and decision; (2) the hearing examiner stage — time the agency temporarily relinquishes control of the case to an examiner until the examiner issues his decision; (3) the agency consideration phase — period of agency consideration looking toward a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dividing time intervals for administrative oversight or reporting, use these three logical divisions to allocate elapsed time to management, examiner, and final-agency-review phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of phases — party's point of view (two basic divisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: From a party's point of view one might consider: (1) how much time after filing before the matter is heard; and (2) how long after that it takes to get a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that reporting and presentation of elapsed time may differ depending on whether the user's interest is managerial (three phases) or litigant-centered (two phases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 5 (1959): time from commencement to completion of evidentiary hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 5 shows how long it took, after a proceeding was commenced, to complete the evidentiary hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This table replaces last year's Table 5 (which measured time to assignment to a hearing examiner); use the hearing-completion rule (last day evidence entered) when populating this table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment measurement choice: assignment to office vs assignment to particular examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables in prior compilations measured time to assignment to a particular examiner; the 1959 compilation measures from assignment to the office of hearing examiners (or chief examiner) because assignment to a particular examiner is often difficult to ascertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use date of assignment to the office of hearing examiners/chief examiner as the anchor for tables measuring examiner-stage intervals unless reliable data exist for assignment to a particular examiner. Include any interval between office assignment and assignment to a particular examiner in reported time intervals (Tables 9, 11, 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 6: time from examiner's initial/recommended decision to agency final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 6 demonstrates the period of time from the examiner's initial or recommended decision to the agency's final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the elapsed time between the examiner's recommended ruling and the agency's final action; report distribution (e.g., percentage over 1 year, over 6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 7: time from 'ripe for agency decision' to agency final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 7 measures the interval from the date the matter was first ripe for agency decision (record certified by examiner, oral argument completed, last brief filed, etc.) to date of issuance of the agency's final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'first ripe for decision' with concrete events (record certified, oral argument completed, last brief filed). Use that anchor to measure agency deliberation time after the public procedures are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts C and D inclusion rule: proceedings in hands of hearing examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts C and D concern only those proceedings reported in Parts A and B which at any time during the year were in the hands of hearing examiners for hearing and decision. If a proceeding had reached the stage where the examiner had issued his decision prior to July 1, it is not reported in the later-year figures for these parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only the portion of proceedings that was actually in the hands of hearing examiners during the reporting period. Exclude matters where the examiner's role had already ended before the reporting-period cutoff even if the agency still had the case on its docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'in the hands of the office of hearing examiners'
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts C and D concern only so much of these proceedings as was in the hands of the office of hearing examiners, from the date the agency turned over the matter to the office or to the chief examiner for hearing and decision, to the time when its pendency before an examiner terminates, whether or not that termination ultimately disposes of the proceeding as far as the agency is concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the turnover date to the office/chief examiner as the start, and the examiner-stage termination as the end, for all examiner-stage duration measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 8 metrics: pending, input, output, and year-end balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 8 gives the number of proceedings of each kind for each agency pending before examiners on July 1 of the years, input during each fiscal year in terms of new cases assigned to the office of hearing examiners and cases remanded or reassigned, examiners' output during each year, and the balance pending at the end of each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count new cases assigned plus remands/reassignments as 'input'; count examiner dispositions (however disposed) as 'output'; compute backlog as beginning pending + input - output = ending pending (watch for reporting discrepancies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude or mark unavailable: certain case types not in Part D
rubrics_metrics.description: Part D reports time-study data for proceedings disposed of by examiners by decisions on the merits after evidentiary hearings. These data are not available for Social Security, Indian probate, and Interstate Commerce Commission cases, except as indicated in the tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag or omit time-study metrics for types of proceedings where underlying data are unavailable or incomplete; document exceptions clearly in the tables and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 9 metric: length of time pending before office of hearing examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 9 measures the period from the date the agency assigned the proceeding to its office of hearing examiners or chief examiner for hearing and decision (rather than assignment to a particular examiner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because assignment to a particular examiner is often shortly after office assignment (with exceptions), use office-assignment date as the consistent anchor. Note exceptions (e.g., NLRB practice) where assignment to a particular examiner may be withheld until shortly before hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include interval between office assignment and particular-examiner assignment in reported intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: It is felt that to the extent there is an interval between assignment to the office of hearing examiners and assignment to a particular examiner, the period thereof should be included in the time intervals reported in Tables 9, 11, and 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude the 'queue' time inside the examiner office; include it when measuring examiner-stage elapsed time for consistency across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 11 metric: overall time in hands of examiners (assignment to office → examiner decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 11 shows the over-all time that such proceedings were in the hands of examiners, from date of assignment of a proceeding to the office of hearing examiners to decision on the merits by an examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure this interval using the office-assignment start date and the examiner-decision date; report distribution (e.g., percent over one year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 12 metric: assignment-to-office → completion-of-evidentiary-hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 12 is a new table to show the length of time which was involved from assignment of a proceeding to the office of hearing examiners to completion of the evidentiary hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hearing-completion rule (last day evidence entered) and the office-assignment date as the anchors; report summary statistics (e.g., 72% completed within 3 months where data available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 13 metric: completion-of-hearing → issuance of examiner's decision; abandonment of 'time under advisement'
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 13 indicates the interval from completion of the evidentiary hearing to issuance of the examiner's decision. Measurement 'time under advisement by examiners' was abandoned because of the difficulty of ascertaining on what date a matter became ripe for examiner decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer measurable anchors (completion of hearing to decision) rather than ambiguous events like 'ripe for decision' when the latter cannot be reliably dated; document the reason for abandoning prior measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 14 metrics: examiner corps, man‑years, average days-in-hearing, average decisions-per-man‑year
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 14 reports examiner counts and grades, man-years of examiner time available (accounting for separations, entrances, inter-agency loans), average number of days per man-year spent presiding over hearings and conferences, and average number of decisions per man‑year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies were asked to report as a day of hearing any day on which the examiner presided over a hearing or conference, whether for the full day or only part of the day, and whether in one proceeding or more than one. Compute average days-in-hearing by dividing total reported hearing-days by man‑years. Compute decisions-per-man‑year by dividing total examiner decisions on the merits after hearing by man‑years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification: cases assigned to examiner for record certification only
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of cases assigned to an examiner with the intention that he not issue a decision, but instead merely conduct the hearing and certify the record to the agency for its decision, is reported in a separate column; these cases are not reported elsewhere in the compilation (except that hearing time is included in hearing-days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify and report 'certify-only' assignments separately; include their hearing-time contribution in hearing-day totals but do not double-count them as examiner decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopened proceedings: statistical handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proceeding, in fact, is reopened, it is added to input just as new cases are, for purposes of these statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat reopened matters as new inputs in annual flow accounting (affects input, output, and backlog calculations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous-compilation metrics considered useful (listed reference metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several tables from previous compilations are of continuing usefulness; listed measures include: (1) Use of 'shortened procedures' (decide on written submissions without oral hearings); (2) Comparison of time for 'shortened procedure' cases vs regular hearing cases; (3) Use of prehearing conferences; (4) Time interval from commencement to assignment to a particular examiner; (5) Time interval from assignment to an examiner to opening of the hearing; (6) Length of hearings; (7) Time interval from close of hearing to final submission to examiner (last brief and proposed findings filed); (8) Time under advisement by examiners; (9) Comparison of withdrawals and dismissals before hearing with number after hearing; (10) Number of proceedings suspended because of interlocutory appeals; (11) Number of proceedings in which hearings were reopened prior to examiner decision; (12) Temporary inter-agency transfers of hearing examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider retaining or reintroducing these measures when feasible; document any methodological changes or reasons for omission (e.g., difficulty of ascertainment for 'time under advisement'). When measuring, use the specific operational definitions used in the prior compilations (or document any changes).
